articleTitle: Numerical study on stall characteristics of a triangular airfoil in low Reynolds number compressible flow
abstract: Due to the low density and low temperature of the atmosphere on the surface of Mars, Mars aircraft are usually in compressible flow at low Reynolds number. In this paper, the dynamic stall characteristics of triangular airfoil with reduced frequencies of 0.09 and 0.15 are studied based on large eddy simulation (LES). The incoming Mach number is 0.5 and the Reynolds number is 3000. The results show that, with the increase of reduced frequency, the lift and drag coefficient in dynamic motion gradually deviates from the static lift and drag coefficient, but the dynamic stall angle of attack has little difference with the static stall angle of attack. In order to obtain the main flow structure during blade dynamic stall, dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) was used to decompose and reconstruct the velocity vector field around the blade. The results show that the DMD decomposition modes mainly include time-average flow field with separation flow at the blade tail, low-frequency large-scale separation flow at the blade leading edge and tail enrolling effect, and high-frequency separation and attachment flow at the blade apex downstream. The first 20 modes reconstruction can basically restore the main flow structure of the flow field.

articleTitle: Wind tunnel's supersonic CD nozzle design and flow analysis
abstract: The objective of this paper is to design and computationally investigate a Mach 5 nozzle. Work involves the development of a 2D MOC program for minimum length nozzle in MATLAB that was used to generate the nozzle contour. CFD analysis was performed on the developed Mach 5 nozzle using ANSYS Fluent for different viscous models including inviscid, laminar and turbulent (k-ε model). The findings of comparable published research on inviscid and turbulent simulations of supersonic CD nozzles were used to validate the CFD technique used in the investigation. Subsequently, the nozzle profile was corrected for boundary layer effects, resulting in an increase in the exit to throat area ratio. Furthermore, the heat generated in the nozzle was examined. Finally, the influence of different ambient pressures and control volume aspect ratios was investigated.

articleTitle: Hydrodynamic characteristics of a surfing paddle-wheel used in high-speed amphibious vehicles
abstract: Conventional amphibious vehicles usually feature a complex propulsion mechanism, low water speed and poor land trafficability, and high energy consumption. To address these concerns, this paper proposes a high-speed propulsion technology suitable for amphibious vehicles and designs a novel paddle-wheel structure by virtue of the theory of high-speed hydrodynamics. In addition, the dynamic characteristics of the surfing paddle-wheel is investigated by using a hydrodynamic approach. The lift force and drag force of the paddle-wheel with different rotation speeds and immersion depths were evaluated. When the paddle-wheel is rotating in water, the relationship among the lift force, rotation speeds and immersion depths of the paddle-wheel was established by using the numerical simulation. The results reveal conclusively that the novel paddle-wheel can drive the relative flow of the water layer when it rotates, producing a considerable upward lifting force, which is positively correlated with immersion depth. The propulsion force decreases with increasing immersion depth, and is negative when the water depth exceeds the wheel centre. As the rotational speed increases, the paddle-wheel is finally lifted out of the water and enters the high-speed surfing state, validating the availability and practicability of the proposed surfing paddle-wheel.

articleTitle: A central-upwind method with interface sharpening technique for compressible multifluid flows
abstract: The computation of the multi-component flow has been attracted a lot of interests owing to several parts of difficulties. The simulation of the interface with the high gradient of physical parameters, the nonconservative model systems and the complexity of the characteristic decompositions are the main problems for the computation of the compressible multifluid flow. We established a central-upwind method with interface sharpening technique based on a unified consistent algorithm proposed recently for the γ-based compressible multifluid flow model to conquer those problems.We derived the consistent boundary velocity based on the scheme we used and we give the justification of the derived scheme. Several numerical results are shown and discussed to demonstrate the ability and the robustness of the proposed method. This work may provide a basic for the computation of the general compressible multicomponent flow problems.

articleTitle: Investigation of cavitation inside the valve plate suction groove of an axial piston pump
abstract: Cavitation produces noise and vibration, which affects the efficiency and service life of the axial piston pump. For the valve plate suction groove of an axial piston pump, cavitation is simulated using DES (Detached Eddy Simulation) turbulent model and mixture multi-phase cavitation model. The cavitation region and vapour volume fraction are compared at different outlet pressures of 60MPa, 40MPa and 30MPa. Also the rotation speed is 2850r/min. The cavitation regions are compared at different contact area between the piston and the groove. The distributions of vapour, velocity and pressure are analysed. The mechanisms of cavitation and reduction are studied. The visual experiment is carried out. It is found that the larger cavitation region due to the higher outlet pressure. The fluid velocity is high, but the pressure is low in the cavitation region. The influence of inlet pressures on cavitation distribution is also discussed. It shows that a reducing cavitation with an increasing inlet pressure. The visual result present that the cavitation generates when the oil flow through the groove.

articleTitle: Numerical study of three-dimensional shock wave/turbulent boundary layer interaction induced by a perpendicular blunt fin
abstract: A numerical study of hypersonic interaction flow induced by a perpendicular blunt fin, which mounted on the flat plate, was performed. Finite volume method and multi-block patched meshes were used to solve three dimensional compressible Reynolds-average equations. The influence of grid density, numerical schemes, limiter functions and turbulent models were also studied. The results shows that the above numerical influencing factors have a huge impact. By comparing with the experimental results, Solutions of the Reynolds averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) equations are unable to predict the heat transfer rate distributions and underestimate the size of separation zone and the heat transfer rate distributions. The results predicted by the delayed detached-eddy simulation (DDES) are in reasonable agreement with the experimental data.

articleTitle: Numerical study on the multiphase flow field of water-entry structure under floating ice environment
abstract: In order to study the influence of the floating ice environment on the multiphase flow field and motion characteristics of structures entering the water, based on the Volume of Fluid multiphase flow model and the overset mesh technique, the numerical simulation of the water-entry structure in a floating ice environment, with the distance between the floating ice and the structure being 1.5D, 2.0D, 2.5D, and 3.0D (D represents the diameter of the structure), and that in an ice-free environment are carried out. The results show that compared with the structure in an ice-free environment, the floating ice has an impact on the movement of the fluid near the free surface, which in turn affects the cavity evolution (including cavity opening, cavity expanding, and cavity closure) during the structure entering the water, but has little impact on the stability of the structure. With the increase of the axis spacing between the floating ice and the structure, the floating ice exerts a declining influence on the cavity evolution, and the structure moves steadily.

articleTitle: Fluidization dynamics and mass transfer in a jet-driven bioreactor for artificial liver system
abstract: Liquid-solid fluidized beds have been applied in the field of bioreactors for artificial liver systems. In this work, the coupling approach of computational fluid dynamics and discrete element method (CFD-DEM) is employed to numerically study the fluidization characteristics and mass transfer mechanism in an impinging-jet-driven bioreactor. The effects of microcapsule density, microcapsule size, and flow rate are investigated. The results show that the bed expansion is proportional to the inlet flow rate and inversely proportional to the microcapsule density and size. The porosity distribution indicates a dead flow zone at the bottom of the bioreactor, which shrinks with the increase of inlet velocity and expands with the increase of microcapsule size and microcapsule density. In addition, the interphase mass transfer model is developed to describe the concentration transport between microcapsules and blood, and explore the mass transfer mechanism.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of heat transfer characteristics for filleted pin fin heat sink in staggered arrangement
abstract: Integrated Chip is widely used in mo dern electronics, and the best performance of these integrated chips depends on effective cooling. So, heat removal from these chips is essential. This work presents heat transfe r enhancement and corresponding pressure drop reduction for filleted pin fin i n staggered arrangement. The results are validated with experimental work. The governing equation solved in this work is e nergy equation. The research is carried out at ANSYS 16.0 software. Heat transfer depends on flow velocity which is associated with di fferent Reynolds numbers. The Reynolds number is taken from 20,000 40,000 for turbulent flow corresponding to velocity 6 10.5 m/s, and the Prandtl number is taken as 0.85. RNG based k turbulence model is used to predict the turbulen t flow parameter. Nusselt number, fin effectiveness and corresponding pressure drop are considered as performance parameters. By using rounded and filleted fins heat transfer surface area increases by 7.24% for which heat transfer enhances about 15%. Also, drag force as well as pressure drop are reduced significantly for filleted fin in staggered flow condition. The fillet improves heat transfer and reduces volume as well as mass of the material, which is economical and practical. Staggered perforation results in more heat transfer than that of only pin fin and perforated pin fin. Finally filleted staggered pin fin of 0.5 mm radius results in maximum Higher Nusselt Number indicates higher heat transfer. It is also found that larger fillet radius such as 0.8 mm fil let radius yields in lower heat transfer than that of 0.5 mm fillet radius but still more than that of pin fins.

articleTitle: Optimization of CD nozzle length for a particular supersonic Mach 5 nozzle
abstract: The objective of this paper was the design of a supersonic nozzle with an exit of Mach number 5 using 2D method of characteristics (MOC) and optimization of its length. A program was developed program for creating minimum length nozzles using the MOC. The program was used to generate the shape of a Mach 5 nozzle. CFD analysis was performed on this nozzle using inviscid, laminar and turbulent (k-ε) viscous models with boundary conditions of 4.005 MPa and 1300 K at the inlet. The findings of comparable published research on inviscid and turbulent simulations of supersonic CD nozzles were used to validate the CFD technique used in the investigation. Subsequently, the nozzle was corrected for boundary layer effects to achieve the target Mach number of 5 under turbulent viscous conditions. This resulted in an increase in its exit to throat area ratio from 25.01 to 27.34. The corrected nozzle's length was reduced by 21 percent with a 2.2 percent decrease in usable area with adequate flow quality as per GJB 4399-2002 nozzle qualifying indices.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of subcooled flow boiling in mini-tube under low pressure and low flow conditions
abstract: Subcooled flow boiling is a common phenomenon in nuclear power systems and highpower density cooling systems. Compared with single-phase flow, subcooled boiling heat transfer coefficient is significantly improved. However, subcooled flow boiling in mini-tubes under low pressure and low flow (LPLF) still needs further study. The numerical study on subcooled flow boiling in mini-tubes in present work is conducted with Eulerian two-fluid approach coupled with the RPI (Rensselae Polytechnic Institute) wall boiling model and is validated by experiment results in a 5.5 mm diameter horizontal tube. The effects of different model parameters on the simulation results are analyzed. The results show that the bubble departure diameter and wall force have certain effects on the local two-phase flow boiling heat transfer coefficient. The numerical results are compared with the experiment in different aspects, the applicability of the model under LPLF conditions is analyzed on this basis.

articleTitle: The effect of water/fuel ratio on heat transfer of supercritical RP-3 with catalytic steam reforming reactions
abstract: Regenerative cooling using endothermic hydrocarbon fuel in mini-channel plays an important role in thermal protection of scramjet engine. In order to further increase the heat transfer efficiency and suppress coke formation, catalytic steam reforming reaction of China aviation kerosene No .3 RP-3 with secondary injection of water is studied. The effect of water in the main inlet on heat transfer characteristics of RP-3 is investigated under different water/fuel ratio (σ), pressure and wall temperature . The results show that with the increase of σ, both the temperature of the flow field and the coke deposition decrease significantly. While the heat transfer coefficient (HTC) increases and the effect of secondary water injection can be gradually strengthened. Compared to σ=10%, when σ is 50% coke deposition decreases by 51.9%, and HTC increases by as much 69.8%. Moreover, it is notable that the decreasing trend of coke content decreases with the increase of σ. There is li mited effect of increase pressure on suppressing coke deposition and enhancing HTC. Compared to low σ, high σ can suppress the coke deposition effectively under high wall temperature condition.

articleTitle: Investigation of spherical bubble dynamics under biological environment based on Rayleigh-Plesset equation
abstract: Cavitation in vivo has a wide range of application prospects in the biomedical field, such as non-invasive lithotripsy, extracorporeal shock wave therapy and target drug delivery. However, the mechanism of the influence of biological environment, such as blood and interstitial fluid, on the bubble.s dynamic behaviour is still not fully revealed. In this work, the kinetic process of spherical symmetric bubble in blood under the action of ultrasonic driving pressure field is investigated based on the classical Rayleigh-Plesset equation. The influences of the liquid viscosity and the surface tension on the bubble dynamical properties are discussed in detail. It is found that liquid viscosity and surface tension have different effects on bubble dynamics, where the viscosity of liquid dominates the attenuation of bubble.s oscillation amplitude, while the surface tension primary influences the responding time of bubble. Since the stronger viscosity and surface tension related to the longer responding time, the oscillation amplitude of the bubble would be significantly smaller in blood than that in water. This study of the dynamical characteristics of bubble in different fluids might help to understand cavitation behaviour in biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Study on hydrodynamic performance of high-speed water-entry for revolutionary body
abstract: A set of method for water-entry at high-speed(≥100m/s) is developed to aim at solving both cavitation and compressible effect for multi-stage flow involving in crossing water-air. The revolutionary body is chosen for computing and the turbulence models including SST k – ω, Standard k – ε, RNG k – ε,and Realizable k – ε are utilized. The cavitation configuration at 1ms is outlined. They are compared with the theoretical results and the results by SST k – ω agree with the theoretical results best. Meanwhile, this set of method is performed for the reference experiment. Compared with experimental results, the set of method is validated in terms of velocity damping and cavitation development. Some different water-entry velocities are regarded as initial condition to be computed. The compressibility of water can not affect the water-entry impact basically with water-entry velocity less than 100m/s. Beyond that, the compressibility of water can put much effect on the water-entry impact, which can lessen the impact and delay the time of peak value. In addition, the cavitation configuration has shrunk, especially in the water-air area. With the increase of water-entry velocity, the velocity damping becomes quicker. The acceleration is relatively higher at the beginning of water-entry. During the period of the model covered by supercavitation, the acceleration gradually declines and changes gently, with the increase of water-entry depth.

articleTitle: Numerical investigation of oscillating flow and heat transfer characteristics in a tapered pulse tube
abstract: This research study presents a comparative analysis of three pulse tube cryocooler models: a base model and two modified models with tapering and divergence at different ends of the pulse tube. The analysis focuses on various flow parameters, including enthalpy, internal energy, static pressure, static temperature, velocity magnitude, mass flow rate, and volume flow rate. The results reveal that the introduction of tapering at the cold end improves heat transfer and enhances cooling efficiency, while divergence at the hot end promotes efficient energy transfer but introduces flow instabilities and pressure fluctuations. The study contributes to the field by highlighting the importance of geometric modifications in pulse tube cryocooler design and offers insights into the underlying mechanisms behind the observed trends. The limitations of the study include its specific operating conditions, and future research directions involve exploring a wider range of parameters, alternative profiles, and system optimization for higher cooling efficiency and reliability. This work paves the way for advancements in pulse tube cryocooler design, aiming for more efficient and reliable cryogenic cooling systems. The results showed that the introduction of tapering and divergence in the pulse tube significantly influenced the flow dynamics, thermodynamic behavior, and cooling performance of the cryocoolers.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of turbulent flow and heat transfer characteristics of a hexalobular pipe
abstract: In this study, numerical analysis of turbulent flow through pipe has been conducted for different shapes of pipe cross-section. The finite element approach has been used to solve three-dimensional steady flow and heat transfer equations with k- . turbulence model. For boundaries ``enhanced wall treatment'' condition has been used in order to evaluate the flow characteristics and heat transfer performance. This study has been conducted for a range of Reynolds number from 6,000 to 15,000. The hexalobular pipe, which is distinct from circular and hexagonal pipes, is the focus of the investigation. Due to it's higher level of turbulence compared to other pipe shapes, the results indicate that hexalobular pipes perform better in heat transfer than circular and hexagonal pipes. However, pressure loss increases with hexalobular shape. The impact of lobe curvature on flow has been evaluated here as well. It emphasizes the importance of considering both the geometry and curvature. The results suggest that with the increase of curvature of lobe, heat transfer increases but the pressure loss also increases. These findings contribute to a better understanding of the relationship between pipe geometry, turbulence, and heat transfer.

articleTitle: Particle dynamics in line plumes
abstract: We present a study on particle dynamics in line plumes with uniform heat flux at the source. We obtain the dimensionless Maxey-Riley equation of particle motion by normalizing the particle motion equation using the near wall length scales of Townsend, 1958. The particle motion is shown to be dependent on the dimensionless numbers, modified Stokes Number (Stm= 0.5(2+ ϵ)CBSt), flux Rayleigh number (Raf = (gβy3Q)/(ναKf)), flux-thermophoretic number (Thf = (2CBCTPrQ)/(〈TP〉Kf)), Prandtl Number (Pr) and gravitation Number (Gn = (1-ϵ)CBSt)/Fr2). The dimensionless plume velocity field are obtained from the similarity solutions of Gebhart, using the same near wall length scales. We then solve the dimensionless Maxey-Riley equation numerically, subjected to this plume velocity field to obtain the flow streamlines and the trajectory of the particles.

articleTitle: Impact of a backward-facing step on oblique transition at Mach 6
abstract: The roughness element has the potential to control transition. The study investigates the impact of a backward-facing step on the oblique transition at Mach 6. The step's height is equal to the local boundary layer thickness. Complete transition processes are simulated by utilizing the implicit large eddy simulation method. The study compares and analyses the transition phenomenon of a backward-facing step to that without a step. In comparison to the oblique transition without a step, the flow with a backward-facing step results in a fundamental second mode transition. Modes decomposition results show that the backward-facing step reduces all instability modes, especially the oblique mode, which should have led to an oblique transition. All the harmonic modes are damped until a 2D disturbance dominates the hypersonic boundary layer flow. The delayed transition is attributed to the accelerated flow at the expansion region. The study indicates that a backward-facing step could be a promising tool for controlling hypersonic transition.

articleTitle: Pressure fluctuation analysis of internal flow field of axial-flow pump based on boundary data immersion method
abstract: Axial-flow pump is a widely used fluid machinery, and the pressure fluctuation in the flow field is the key factor affecting its stable operation. The pressure fluctuation can cause the vibration and noise of the pipe and accessories. The purpose of this paper is to reveal the pressure pulsation characteristics of the unsteady flow field in axial-flow pumps. The relationship between the flow and pressure pulsation of the axial-flow pump was analyzed by the numerical approach with Immersed Boundary Data Method. For the turbulence closure mode, Large-eddy simulation (LES) is employed to the numerical simulation of the unsteady flow field of the axial-flow pump. Due to suction, there is a significant low pressure near the shroud at the impeller inlet. In the low-pressure part of the impeller outlet, a significant low pressure occurs in the middle of the blade. The pressure fluctuation amplitude of the impeller inlet section is larger than that of the impeller outlet. At the impeller outlet, the middle of the blade occurs back-flow phenomenon because of the differences in pressure distribution. The distribution of pressure is more disordered at span 50% of the impeller outlet, resulting in an obvious variation in the pressure pulsation amplitude.

articleTitle: Numerical study on DDT detonation under supersonic injection mixing conditions
abstract: This study employs dynamic adaptive grid refinement technique to solve the Navier-Stokes equations with the chemical reaction source term, performing numerical simulation on the phenomenon of detonation combustion and coupling the process of combustion in the chamber with flow mixing. The research focuses on a rapid DDT (Deflagration to Detonation Transition) mode ignited at the rear of the detonation tube. Based on realistic injection mixing conditions and without introducing external disturbances, rapid explosion in the smooth tube is achieved, and the effect of ignition jet injection pressure on rapid explosion is investigated. The results show that strong turbulence promotes the interaction between shockwaves and flames, leading to the initiation of explosion, and the DDT transition can be attributed to the reaction-gradient mechanism. The nonuniform distribution of fuel significantly affects the wavefront structure of the detonation wave, revealing two distinct types of detonation wavefronts: those that are perpendicular to the upper and lower walls (known as normal detonation wavefronts), and those that are at a slant angle with respect to the upper and lower walls (known as oblique detonation wavefronts). The oblique detonation wavefronts are generated as a result of the interaction between the detonation wave and the boundary layer flame.

articleTitle: Numerical investigation of the six degrees of freedom hydrodynamic performance of a sailboat in wave conditions
abstract: The hydrodynamic characteristics of sailboats in varying sea conditions are crucial for controlling the boats and complete the required movements. This paper investigates the six-element forces of Laser Radial sailboats under oblique sailing with first-order waves. Numerical calculations employing the overlapping mesh technique and DFBI model provide insights into the sailboat's details. The study reveals significant findings: speed has a dominant influence on resistance, accounting for approximately 64% of the total. Wavelength factors contribute about 12%, while amplitude factors contribute about 24% at an 8-degree heel angle. As speed increases, resistance intensifies. Additionally, wavelength impacts the longitudinal pitching moment more obviously, while wave amplitude has a larger impact on the yawing moment.

articleTitle: Numerical study on the flow field for deep-sea hydrothermal plume tracking simulation
abstract: In this paper, the distribution of hydrothermal buoyancy plume in the deep-sea environment is studied numerically. Submarine hydrothermal vents are prominent manifestations of hydrothermal activities and are of great scientific and engineering importance. It is an important basis to obtain the temporal and spatial distribution information of different hydrothermal plumes for tracking and locating the source of hydrothermal plumes. Based on Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes equations and Realizable k-ε turbulence model, the plumes of hydrothermal vents at depths of 800 m, 1200 m, and 1400 m were calculated and studied to obtain the spatial distribution of variables such as velocity field, temperature field and turbulent kinetic energy. The research results of this paper provide an important basis for the simulation of deep-sea hydrothermal plume tracking based on autonomous underwater vehicles.

articleTitle: Numerical investigation on the instability of a two-dimensional free shear layer
abstract: In this paper, the challenging problem of the instability of a two-dimensional free shear layer is studied using direct numerical simulation. Following the experiment of Schubauer and Skramstad (JAS 1947) that produced the classical data on boundary-layer instability, we adopt a similar way to introduce a sinusoidal disturbance upstream of the simulated free shear layer. Upon reaching a fully developed state, the velocity fluctuation along the centreline of the shear layer is plotted to determine the instability growth rate, based on which the stability nature of stable, unstable, or neutral can be determined. To pursue a diagram in terms of the dimensionless wave number vs. Reynolds number, which is typically used to differentiate the stable and unstable regimes, we explore a variety of cases with different shear layer intensities, fluid viscosities, and disturbance frequencies. As a result, all neutral cases are identified and plotted in the neutral stability curve, showing a general agreement with the theoretical curve for Re up to 36. Considering that the relevant theoretical result was obtained decades ago by solving the Orr-Sommerfeld equation, this work represents an effort to resort to numerical simulation for theory validation, which is otherwise difficult by means of experiment.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of a spinning missile with dithering canards
abstract: In the paper, the structural overset grid method was used to generate the computational grid. The flow field of the spinning missile with dithering canards was numerically simulated and the interference characteristics caused by the missile rotation and the canards deflection were analyzed. The results show that the canard vortex propagates backward along the direction of the incoming flow and decays continuously. The rotation effect causes the canard vortex to tilt in the opposite direction to the missile spinning direction compared to the non-spinning case. The vortex strength is stronger in the case of rotation than that in the case of no rotation. With the increase of the span length, the rudder tip vortex gradually moves away from the missile body, the vortex strength decreases and the influence on the body and the fins weakens. Because the rudder tip vortex moves away from the missile body, the influence of the rotation effect of the missile on it weakens and the inclination degree of the vortex decreases.

articleTitle: Bulk rise in the interstices of capillaries
abstract: In this paper, we measured the capillary rise in the interstices created when three circular capillaries were joined together. We used different sizes of circular capillaries with outer diameters of 700 μm, 1380 μm, 5000 μm and 10000 μm and focused on the bulk meniscus rise. We found two distinct phases during the capillary rise, a visco-inertial regime and a visco-gravitational regime. To complement our experimental findings, we propose a novel scaling analysis for the capillary bulk meniscus growth in these regimes. In the visco-inertial regime, we developed the relation as h2(t)=(2b/a)(t-(1/a)(1-exp(-at))), where a= (μπ)/(ρR2) and b= (πσcosθ)/(ρR). While in visco-gravitational regime, we find the solution as h(t)=(2c/d)(1+W(-exp(-1-d2t/c))) where, c= (σcosθ)/(ρ) and d = (ρgR2)/(πμ) and W is the Lambert function. We found that the experimental data collapses on to the analytical solution which was plotted in dimensionless form. We now have a better understanding of the dynamics of capillary bulk rise in interstices, which has significant repercussions for a variety of processes, both natural and industrial.

articleTitle: Numerical study of dynamic shock wave closed-loop control by arc plasma
abstract: The supersonic flow fluctuation caused by dynamic shock/boundary layer interaction brings great challenges to aerodynamic design and stability control of aircraft. The mechanism of dynamic shock wave closed-loop control by arc plasma is numerically studied. The dynamic shock wave is formed by a rotating inclined ramp in supersonic flow. The closed-loop control model is established based on the pressure ratio across the dynamic shock at monitor point with using Proportion Integration (PI) control method. It achieves a stable shock pressure ratio with the error between averaged value and the target value less than 0.1% when the ramp angle ranges from 7° to 9°. It also shows that the overshoot of the pressure ratio across the dynamic shock does not exceed 2.0% of the target value and the standard deviation is less than 0.3%. It verifies the effectiveness for the dynamic shock wave closed-loop control based on the arc plasma model, and realizes a stable flow downstream the dynamic shock.

articleTitle: Influence of laser thickness on the determination of solid volume fraction in refraction index matching experiments
abstract: Refraction index matching (RIM) method is widely used in the studies of the particle-liquid flows. However, the determination of the solid volume fraction ϕ based on the RIM imaging indicators has not been well studied. Based on discrete element methods and virtual sampling and projection process, this paper studies the influence of the laser thickness on the prediction models of ϕ and the model parameters based on the area fraction c2D and the size of the Voronoi diagram dpoly. It is found that the traditionally used proportional function of c2D-ϕ holds only when the laser thickness H is infinitely small. When H is not negligible compared to the particle size, a linear model should be adopted whose intercept increases with H. The variation of the model parameters based on dpoly under different H is also obtained and the exponent agrees well with the experimental result.

articleTitle: Evaluation of heat transfer and melting process of a PCM inside a trapezoidal shape enclosure
abstract: The thermal performance of phase change material (PCM) is significant to latent heat thermal energy storage applications. This paper's current effort is given to investigate the heat transfer pattern and melting process of a PCM (tin) inside a trapezoidal shape enclosure. This study aims to enhance heat transmission and verify the applicability of PCM in thermal storage facilities. The finite element technique is used to examine the transient heat transfer of the system numerically. The enclosure is initially filled with a portion of solid tin, and the remaining is liquid tin. Constant heat flux and fixed temperature are used as heat source and sink, respectively. The result includes qualitative visualizations of temperature and velocity distributions and quantitative thermal responses at a fixed point for relative comparison between PCM and liquid tin. The use of PCM is found advantageous in heat transfer improvement.

articleTitle: Visualization of shock-free compression/laminar boundary layer interaction caused by a curved fin in supersonic flow
abstract: The laminar boundary layer interacting with a curved fin is visualized in a Mach 2.95 flow. The nanoparticle-based planar laser scattering (NPLS) method, which has a high spatiotemporal resolution, is used to obtain the fine flow structures of the shock-free compression/laminar boundary layer interaction. A curved fin of a 20-degree total turn produces shock-free compression in the investigated region. The visualization results reveal the separation of the boundary layer flow and the downwards flowing of the high-momentum mainstream. The flowfield is divided into three regions. The disturbance of the vortexes shed from the fin combined with the pressure gradients attributed to the transition of the boundary layer. The vortexes with variable scales, generated from the flow on the fin, shed from the upstream flow on the fin and developed from the boundary layer, respectively, spread over the downstream convergence region.

articleTitle: Thin film below a moving drop
abstract: The motion of an immiscible viscous drop on a surface in another viscous medium is determined by the nature of the thin film that forms between the drop and the surface; we study the thickness of such a film. The problem is characterized by the ratio of gravitational to capillary forces Bo (Bond number), the ratio of viscous to capillary forces Ca (capillary number), angle of inclination α, and viscosity ratio λ. We focus on low values of Bo, where the undeformed drop surface has an almost spherical shape due to the high capillary forces. To find the film thickness, the thin film is modeled according to the lubrication approximation, solved numerically, and matched with the perturbed spherical surface of the drop at the transition region between them. It is assumed that a constant shear stress acts on the film due to the drop. The curvature of the thin film in the transition region was found to be equal to that of a Landau-Levich film, where the fluid is dragged vertically by a moving plate, which is independent of α, λ, and Bo. The dependence of the film thickness on α, λ, and Bo is introduced by the curvature of the spherical surface, whose curvature is found by normal stress balance using leading order approximation in terms of Ca. The dimensionless film thickness hf was found to be majorly dependent on Ca as hf~Ca(2/3) and only at high values of Ca, hf was dependent on λ and α. The theory has been compared with experimental measurements of film thickness and existing numerical simulations. A good agreement is found for drops with lower values of Bo, which are spherical and move slowly.

articleTitle: Hysteretic behaviors of shock waves during the pitching motion of airfoil
abstract: Airfoil's performance is greatly influenced by the compressibility of the flow, which is generally expressed by the Mach number. This article analyzes the effect of Mach number on the pressure distribution and aerodynamic coefficients of the NACA 0012 airfoil at a constant Reynolds number of 5.5E6 in steady and pitching conditions. A Roe's density-based model is used with the k-ω SST turbulence model and the unsteady and compressible Navier-Stokes equations. Since shocks and unsteady effects are present, temporal and spatial discretization is carried out with 2nd order accuracy. A comparison between the stationary and pitching airfoil results and the available numerical and experimental data has been conducted to ensure the solver performance's accuracy. According to the steady solution, as compressibility increases, the shock becomes stronger and approaches the trailing edge. Based on the pitching airfoil results, compressibility significantly impacts the extent of the hysteresis loop so that the difference between the lift and moment coefficients in the airfoil return paths increases with an increase in Mach number.

articleTitle: Unsteady numerical simulation of jet interaction by coupling aerodynamics and flight dynamics
abstract: Aiming at the influence of motion conditions on the aerodynamic disturbance of reaction control jet control, an unsteady aerodynamic/motion integration method is established based on the Reynolds-averaged N-S equation. Numerical simulation of the ruddered missile controlled by the direct force of the lateral jet reaction is numerically simulated, the detailed structural characteristics of the jet instantaneous disturbance flow field are discussed, the force and moment coefficients and the time-varying characteristics of the aircraft state are analyzed. The calculated comparison results between the unsteady state and the steady state are analyzed. The research results show that the attitude-controlled jet has strong unsteady characteristics when the aircraft moves, and the normal force amplification factor and disturbing pitch moment calculated in steady state are higher than those calculated in unsteady motion.

articleTitle: Modelling of particle separation in pulsing air flow
abstract: We consider here the implementation of dry coal beneficiation using air jigging technology, to investigate the Design of air jigging laboratory equipment for testing of multi-component separation of granular materials (coal) and simulations with coupling ANSYS FLUENT and EDEM. The study explores the influence of different flow velocity (8-12 m/s) and pulsations (4π, 6π, 8π). In simulation there are 10000 solid particles with densities 800 kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, 1600 kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, respectively, with size 3 mm. Some good result of calculation is when flow velocity 11 m/s and its pulsations 6π. Experiments were conducted with a coal from Mongolian Ömnögovi Province Tavantolgoi mining camp in the size range from 1-5 mm and when the in rotation of air flow valve when frequency was 1.83 Hz, was the best separation.

articleTitle: Tomographic PIV investigation of thermal plumes in turbulent convection
abstract: Understanding flux scaling in turbulent convection requires detection and characterization of thermal plumes. Hence, we investigate near-wall thermal plumes in turbulent convection using a 3D velocity field obtained in a 4 mm thick volume using Tomographic Particle Image Velocimetry (Tomo-PIV) with Rayleigh number Ra<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</sub>=1.71×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> and Prandtl number Pr=6.23. Plumes are detected in numerous horizontal planes parallel to the bottom hot plate using the negative horizontal divergence criterion (∇<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</sub>. u<0) [Shevkar et al. 2022, J. Fluid Mech., 941]. An experimentally obtained 3D velocity data shows that plume regions mostly take positive values of vertical velocity. We also found a strong correspondence between the values of the negative horizontal divergence and that of the negative dominant eigenvalue of 2D strain rate tensor λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</sub> in several horizontal planes at various vertical locations. In addition, we demonstrate that these line plumes are also instantaneous Lagrangian coherent structures (LCS) in the instantaneous limit. We also discuss the attracting structures visualised using backward time Lyapunov exponent in the instantaneous limit

articleTitle: A solution of teaching CFD to link study and research
abstract: The expanding applications of computational fluid mechanics (CFD) in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, environmental engineering require researchers with both self-learning and code development abilities. With the aim of teaching upper grade undergraduate students and young graduate students both mathematical theory and practice abilities, Beijing Institute of Technology (BIT) is carrying out a novel implementation of CFD education including fundamental algorithm, code skill, basic example and application development in the framework of hyperbolic system framework. The fundamental elements of advection in both incompressible and compressible fluid flow are extracted as a unified part to teach. In theory, one dimensional (1D) advection equation could be generalized to 1D hyperbolic system such as Euler equation and two dimensional (2D) convection equation, and finally be generalized to high dimensional system of fluid flow. Therefore, the teaching of numerical skills in 1D advection almost forms the most important aspect and a first step in learning CFD. Students will learn time marching scheme, numerical flux calculation and space reconstruction technique, with both mathematical inductions on boards and code development with one basic code written in Fortran given by the teacher. With all those together, students will easily generalize their knowledge, numerical and coding skills to 1D system, 2D convection equation, and even high dimensional systems. Education experience tells that undergraduate students could master basic elements of CFD, and graduate students could extend the fundamental algorithm to other system in research level.

articleTitle: Flow loss mechanisms investigation on a novel corotating scroll expander for supercritical carbon dioxide power system
abstract: The expander is the critical component of supercritical CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (S-CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) Brayton cycle power generation systems. The paper proposed an innovative design for a high-speed co-rotating scroll expander and created a 3D CFD transient simulation model to investigate its flow characteristics and loss mechanisms. Entropy production theory and omega vortex identification method were utilized to analyze the primary regions and causes of flow losses during different working processes of the co-rotating scroll expander. The results showed that flow losses of the co-rotating expander mainly occurred during the suction and discharge processes. During the suction process, the disturbance by the two scroll tips resulted in prominent vortex structures, leading to significant irreversible losses. During the expansion process, the fluid flow in the expansion chamber is relatively stable due to the synchronous and co-directional rotation of the two scrolls, resulting in only small irreversible losses. During the discharge process, separated flow at the area behind the scroll tails, mixing working fluids between the discharge and back pressure chamber, caused substantial irreversible losses. The study provided theoretical guidance for optimizing flow control in the co-rotating scroll expander used in S-CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> Brayton cycle power generation systems.

articleTitle: Numerical study on the performance of NACA 4412 airfoil with insertion of tangential internal slot
abstract: Controlling flow separation is one of the most important techniques for reducing drag and increasing the lift-to-drag ratio. The aim of this study is to enhance the aerodynamic performance of NACA 4412 airfoil through passive method of controlling flow separation. Accordingly, the geometry of airfoil has been modified with tangential internal slots. The commencement of each slot is kept constant at 0.05 chord (C) from the leading edge. The exit positions of the slots are varied vertically at 0.4C slot exit. So, two parameters have been varied: slot width and vertical slot exit position. The angles of attack (AoA) are varied from 0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> to 26<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> with 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> increments for every parameter with a fixed Reynolds number of 1.6×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>. Pressure-based solver and k-ω. SST model are used for analysis. For all the slot configurations, better aerodynamic performance in terms of lift-to-drag ratio occurs at the moderately higher angles of attack. Among the vertical exit position, the lowermost position shows better aerodynamic performance. Tapered slot having slot exit width 2%C has higher lift-to-drag ratio than that of the other configurations from AoA 6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> to the end. However, the highest lift-to-drag ratio is found at AoA 8<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> for all the modified designs whereas it happens at AoA 6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> for the airfoil with no slot. Moreover, for this configuration, the stalling angle of attack is delayed to AoA 24<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> whereas for other configurations the stall angle gradually decreases and for no slot it is the lowest which is AoA 16<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>.

articleTitle: Numerical study on the flow field of a transverse jet in supersonic crossflow
abstract: The flow field of a transverse jet in supersonic crossflow, which is typically encountered inside a supersonic combustor, is numerically simulated in the present study by solving the Reynolds-Averaged Navier Stokes (RANS) equations with the SST k-ω model. The combustor entrance is configured to enter finite parallel streams of air, followed by a rearward-facing step. Gaseous jets of hydrogen are injected transversely from the opposite walls of the combustor. Combustors of three different widths, i.e., 40 mm, 50 mm, and 60 mm, with the fuel injection pressures varying according to the jet-to-crossflow pressure ratios (PR) of 4.5, 9.0, 13.5, and 18.0 are considered for the present investigation. Flow features such as the change in height and width of the barrel shock, the bow shock angle, the location of two opposite bow shocks' interaction, and the position of the separation bubble are analyzed from the simulated results. The effects of the change in the flow features on the mixing performance inside the combustor are quantified by calculating the mixing efficiency at the combustor exit.

articleTitle: Effects of microstructures on the performance in the supersonic regime
abstract: To predict the drag reduction with modified microstructures, a numerical method based on the Menter SST turbulence model and riblet boundary modelling method is proposed. Based on the classical experimental data of microstructures with symmetric V grooves, an intensive study on the drag reduction is established in complex flow conditions. Finally, an overall design and evolution of drag reduction by modifying the microstructure is given in the case of the wave rider configuration.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of the effects of size ratio and relative position on two self-propelled foils in tandem arrangement
abstract: The effects of size ratio and relative position on the hydrodynamic performance of two self-propelled foils with tandem arrangement in incompressible flows were numerically investigated. Simulations were performed with the immersed boundary method (IBM), and the foils are modelled with the NACA0012 foils. Based on a systematic parameter study of the size ratio and relative position between the two foils, the swimming velocity and propulsion efficiency are discussed in detail. Vortex structures of flow field are analysed to elucidate the flow-mediated interaction. The results showed that foils do not always benefit from the hydrodynamic interaction between each other, and the size ratio has an important influence on the selection of foils' relative position to form a thrust-enhancement or energy-efficiency propulsion pattern. The smaller the size ratio, the greater the hydrodynamic benefits follower foil can obtain. As the size ratio increasing, leader foil may achieve smaller power consumption with faster forward velocity.

articleTitle: Mixed convection of a power-law fluid in a square enclosure with an oscillating cylinder
abstract: A two-dimensional in-house numerical solver has been employed to study laminar flow in an in-line oscillating cylinder with constant wall temperature inside a square enclosure. Due to the oscillations of the cylinder, forced convection is set-up along with natural convection inside the power law fluid. Ghost Cell Immersed Boundary Method (GCIBM) is employed to handle the moving boundary. Effect of various parameters such as, Richardson number, Keulegan-Carpenter number and Reynolds number, on the power law fluid is studied. The flow physics of the problem has been investigated with the help of isotherms, streamlines and vorticity contours. The flow-field is quantified with the help of time-averaged Nusselt number.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of jet interference at full angle of attack for slender body
abstract: The jet interference characteristics of a slender body are numerically simulated at full angle of attack by solving Navier-Stokes equations. Based on the simulation results, the pressure distribution and flow field structure of typical section are studied. The jet interference distribution and jet amplification factor on the lateral jet flow of a slender body at full angle of attack are analyzed under different inflow parameters and jet flow parameters. The results show that: The jet interference amplification factor have larger fluctuation at the range of full attack angle with bigger flight Mach number and lower flight altitude; when the jet flow is in different rolling attitude angles, the interference characteristics change differently; when the angle of attack close to 90°, the jet interference changes sharply.

articleTitle: Effect of inner shear layer on the formation of central recirculation zone in a V-shaped swirling flame
abstract: This paper numerically studies the formation of the central recirculation zone (CRZ) in a V-shaped premixed swirling flame. The results show that decreasing the equivalence ratio (Φ) or increasing the Reynolds number (Re) would facilitate the emergence of CRZ, which is accompanied by an enhanced inner shear layer (ISL). It can be understood from the vortex-dynamics point of view that the CRZ grows as the vorticity in the ISL accumulates rapidly and induces velocity opposite to the main swirling jet. By calculating the ISL local intensity, γ, as a function of the streamwise location, we find that the ISL intensity first increases and then decreases. The maximum γ decreases with increasing Φ , whereas it increases with increasing Re. The source terms in the vorticity transport equation are analyzed to reveal the mechanism influencing the ISL intensity and the resultant CRZ. Specifically, both effects of vortex stretching/tilting and baroclinic torque contribute to vorticity growth in the ISL, whereas the thermal dilation and vorticity diffusion cause the ISL intensity to decay. The present study sheds light on the possibility of CRZ regulation in swirl combustion by controlling the vorticity transportation in the ISL.

articleTitle: The flow dynamics and instabilities of viscoelastic liquid film under the effect of gravity and external air-flow shear
abstract: The flow dynamics of upper-convected-Maxwell(UCM) liquid film flowing down a vertical rigid wall was considered. In addition to the effect of gravity, external air-flow shear was considered. This article presents a set of evolution equations that are valid for moderately incompressible viscoelastic liquid films based on integral theory. The effects of gravity and external air-flow shear were considered simultaneously. The linear instability of the system was examined using a normal-mode analysis. This shows that the external air-flow shear and viscoelasticity can both destabilize the falling film, and the effect of the external air-flow shear is much more evident. When the friction of the external air-flow exceeds, the high-frequency fluctuations become drastic to some extent. On the other hand, in order to investigate the wave generation mechanism preliminary, the constant initial and boundary conditions are applied. The results show that there was no wave generation with a constant initial and boundary and zero air friction. However, when air friction occurs, waves occur, and the frequency of the wave increases with air friction. Viscoelasticity can only increase the disability of the liquid film, which is not the reason for the wave generation.

articleTitle: Influence analysis of turbulence on finite rate surface catalytic effects
abstract: The Menter's SST κ-ω turbulence model and a finite rate surface catalytic reaction model considering the adsorption, desorption, E-R reaction and L-H reaction mechanisms are used to study the turbulence and surface catalysis coupling effects. Turbulent and laminar flow fields around a 1 m length blunt wedge with a half-apex angle of 10° under different surface catalytic conditions were simulated. By comparing and analyzing the laminar and turbulent heating data at x=0.95m along the wedge under finite rate catalytic condition, it is found that turbulence enhances both convective heat flux and diffusive heat flux, and the diffusive heat flux increment accounts for 5.8% of the total heat flux increment. The influence of the flight Mach number and altitude on the turbulent/surface catalytic coupling effects was also studied. The results show that the increase of the flight Mach number and flight altitude both increase the fraction of diffusive heat flux increment to total heat flux increment. The analysis indicates that the increase of Mach number enhances the dissociation of N2, and the higher flight height also produces more N behind the shock due to the higher free stream temperature. In both circumstances turbulence transports more nitrogen to the wall, which increases the ratio of N to O concentration, and promotes the recombination of NO.

articleTitle: Effects of wall roughness on the cellular pattern evolution and failure of gaseous detonations
abstract: In this study, the effects of rough-walled tubes on the propagation and failure of gaseous detonation are being investigated numerically. When a cellular detonation propagates in a tube with rough-wall boundary conditions, apart from the losses, its unstable cellular frontal structure is significantly modified due to gasdynamic perturbations by the rough wall, resulting in velocity deficit (or the presence of a quasi-detonation) and eventually failure. The latter is the focus of this study, i.e., how are the intrinsic cellular pattern of the detonation and its reacting gasdynamic flow fields changed by the presence of wall roughness? To simplify the computational modelling effort while revealing some salient unstable characteristics of cellular detonations propagating in rough tubes, the strategy adopted in this study is to conduct numerical simulations using an ideal-gas, reactive flow model given by the inviscid Euler equations with a simplified two-step chemical kinetic model. The effects of the chemical sensitivity of the combustible mixture, channel width, and various degrees of roughness using different obstacle sizes on the intrinsic cellular detonation instability and propagation limits are investigated through a detailed parametric study.

articleTitle: Investigating ship airwake on a moving ship model
abstract: We investigated the turbulent flows on the moving deck of a scaled NATO Generic Destroyer model. The measurements were performed in a large wind-wave interaction facility, allowing the simulation of natural pitching motion. Planar Particle Image Velocimetry was used to obtain the flow structures and the turbulent airwake characteristics on the deck. The results show that the airwake characteristics are strongly affected by both the ship position and its moving direction. The ship-induced velocity directly impacts the flow, inducing strong downwash over the landing deck when the deck is descending around its neutral position. In this study, we divided the ship motion cycle into 8 phases to identify the associated turbulent airwake features, leading to the assessment of the landing safety during different stages of the ship motion. By employing a specified threshold for the standard deviation of the vertical velocity (σw), we found that the helicopter will be more likely to encounter extreme turbulent motions with negative pitch angle at typical high hover height on the landing deck. The reverse applies when the helicopter hovers at a higher elevation.
